messages.author: 02ba30432f1e7871
messages.subject: y axis label centering
parts:
Hello,

I have a bar chart with the x tick labels rotated 90 deg. When the
labels are long, the y axis title is noticeably off center (relative
to the plot area). I can manually adjust it with:
axis.title.y = theme_text(angle=90, hjust = .6)
however, the plot is produced via a script with dynamic data inputs,
so the x-axis category names may not be the same each time. Is there a
way to dynamically center the y axis title on a plot? Or, better, is
there a way to center the y-axis title relative to the plot area
rather than the entire graph area?

Thanks,
Jon

Code to reproduce the effect is here:

Country = c("United Kingdom","United Kingdom","United
Kingdom","France","France","France","Germany","Germany","Germany","Belgium","Belgium","Belgium","Spain","Spain","Spain")
Position =
c("Net","Long","Short","Net","Long","Short","Net","Long","Short","Net","Long","Short","Net","Long","Short")
Weight =
c(0.017529466,0.262378674,-0.244849208,-0.005933642,0.148120651,-0.154054294,-0.017165164,0.138839288,-0.156004452,0.021277306,0.05011526,-0.028837955,0.015117215,0.067420154,-0.052302939)
fund <- data.frame(Country, Position, Weight)

p <- ggplot(fund,aes(Country, Weight, fill=Position)) +
geom_bar(position="dodge")
# y-axis title is centered here:
print(p)

p <- p + opts(axis.text.x = theme_text(angle=90,hjust=1))
# y-axis title is off-center here:
print(p)

messages.author: 439a20c9d67ff394
messages.subject: Re: y axis label centering
parts:
The only option I know of at the moment is to manually pad your axis
label strings with leading or trailing whitespace. I don't know enough
grid functionality to know if its possible to write a function that
detects the size of the offset and adds the correct amount of padding
automatically; I suspect not, or someone would have suggested it by
now.
